Question: Five runners, \(P,\) \(Q,\) \(R,\) \(S,\) \(T,\) have a race, and \(P\) beats \(Q,\) \(P\) beats \(R,\) \(Q\) beats \(S,\) and \(T\) finishes after \(P\) and before \(Q.\) Who could not have finished third in the race?
Solution:
The conditions place \(P,T,Q,S\) in that order: \(P\) finishes before \(T\), \(T\) before \(Q\), and \(Q\) before \(S\). Also, \(P\) finishes before \(R\).

Consequently, \(P\) is ahead of all four other runners and must be first. The three runners \(P,T,Q\) are ahead of \(S\), so \(S\) must be fourth or fifth. Neither \(P\) nor \(S\) can be third.

To check the remaining runners, the following orders, written from first to last, satisfy every condition:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&P,T,Q,R,S &&\text{puts }Q\text{ third},\\
&P,T,R,Q,S &&\text{puts }R\text{ third},\\
&P,R,T,Q,S &&\text{puts }T\text{ third}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus exactly \(\boxed{P\text{ and }S}\) could not have finished third, choice \(\text{C}\).
